attributes.cardDescription: A Position's interview loop content — an ordered, reorderable list of rounds, each carrying a round type and its markdown interview questions
attributes.readMe:
# Interview Plan

## Summary
The interview *content* for one `Position`: a `position` (linksTo), a `createdDate`, and `rounds` (containsMany `InterviewPlanRoundField` — see interview-plan.gts: `roundType` an `InterviewRoundField`, `questions` a `MarkdownField`). Array order IS loop order — there is no separate integer `order` field; resequencing the loop means reordering the `rounds` array itself. `title` is computed as `Interview Plan — {position.title}`.

## Import
```ts
import { InterviewPlan, InterviewPlanRoundField, INTERVIEW_ROUND_COLORS } from './interview-plan';
```

## Usage — three or more ways this is used

**1. Created and populated by AI.** `GenerateInterviewQuestionsCommand`
(commands/generate-interview-questions-command.gts) finds-or-creates the
linked Position's `interviewPlan` on first use, then upserts (replaces if the
same `roundType` already exists, otherwise appends) the round it just
generated questions for. Running it three times for phone-screen, technical
and onsite builds the plan round by round.

**2. Manually authored or edited by a hiring manager.** The same isolated
view that shows AI-generated rounds is directly editable — a manager can
write or revise a round's `questions` by hand without ever running the AI
command, and reorder rounds with the move up/down controls next to each
round. Nothing about the card requires AI involvement; it is a plain
structured record first, an AI output second.

**3. Referenced read-only from a Meeting.** `Meeting.interviewPlanRound`
(meeting.gts) looks up `this.candidate?.position?.interviewPlan?.rounds` for
the round whose `roundType` matches the Meeting's own `roundType`, so an
interviewer opening a scheduled Meeting sees exactly the questions written
for the round they're about to run, under an "Interview questions (this
round)" heading — without leaving the Meeting to go find the Position.

**4. As `Position.interviewPlan`.** The Position's own isolated view renders
an "Interview Plan" panel (`<@fields.interviewPlan @format='embedded' />`) so
a recruiter reviewing the requisition can see the whole loop's shape from one
place, or an empty-state prompt if none exists yet.

## Template Usage
Isolated view renders an ordered `<ol>` of rounds, each showing a
color-coded round-type pill (`INTERVIEW_ROUND_COLORS`, distinct hues from
CANDIDATE_STAGE_COLORS/MEETING_TYPE_COLORS since this classifies a plan
round's content, not a candidate's stage or a meeting's type) and a questions
preview, plus move up/down buttons (disabled at the array boundaries) that
reorder `rounds` in place and save via `SaveCardCommand`. Embedded/fitted show
a compact round-count + position summary.

**Example in use:** `InterviewPlan/178f4bd9-d637-4c5a-aae2-96eec26fbbd0`,
linked from `Position/platform-engineer`, carries four rounds (phone-screen,
technical, onsite, final) with real markdown question sets, and
`Meeting/interview-tomas` (roundType `final`) demonstrates a scheduled
Meeting reading its own round's questions back from this plan.

**Boundary — not a scheduling tool.** InterviewPlan owns round *content*
(what to ask), never round *timing* (when it happens, who attends, what got
scored) — that is entirely `Meeting`'s job (`date`, `interviewers`,
`interviewScore`, `scorecard`). A Position can have exactly one InterviewPlan
but many scheduled Meetings against it, one per candidate per round.

**Non-goals:** scheduling or calendar integration; per-candidate
customization of a round's questions (the plan is per-Position, shared across
every candidate in that pipeline); scoring or feedback capture (Meeting's
`scorecard`/`interviewScore` own that).
